questions.question: According to the scope statement of TR65, at what point does the technology transfer (TT) defined in this report end?

options.A: When the PPQ batches are completed and Quality releases the first process validation batch
options.B: When regulatory approval is obtained and the process is handed over to the operations team
options.C: When the regulatory submission is filed and accepted
options.D: When the first commercial batch is shipped to the target market

questions.explanation: TR65 states clearly that the TT in this report ends with handover to the operations team after regulatory approval. Completion of PPQ, acceptance of the filing, or the first shipment all occur before or after this point and are not the endpoint set by TR65.

questions.question: According to the TR65 Glossary, what does Facility Fit Assessment refer to?

options.A: An assessment of the SU's historical batch data and process capability to confirm they are sufficient to support scale-up
options.B: An assessment of the MAH's financial capability toward the RU and the contract terms, to confirm that the supply agreement is feasible
options.C: An assessment of the maturity of the RU's quality system and its GMP mindset, as due diligence before an audit
options.D: An assessment of the RU's manufacturing capability, considering equipment, design, capacity, and the risks of bringing the product into the facility

questions.explanation: A Facility Fit Assessment is an assessment of the manufacturing capability of the receiving unit (RU), covering equipment, design, capacity, and the risks associated with bringing the product into that facility. Assessing the RU's quality system is Quality's due diligence, and assessing SU data or financial terms is not the definition of this term.

questions.question: A product has entered Phase 3 clinical trials, and the company plans to transfer it to a commercial manufacturing site. Which type of TT is this, and what are its characteristics?

options.A: Development-commercial; the full range of CMC requirements is transferred, with the goal of establishing comparability between the SU and the RU
options.B: Clinical-clinical; focused on CMC appropriate to that phase, with TR65 describing its requirements item by item in detail with examples, and requiring full validation
options.C: Commercial-commercial; the original manufacturing site provides full CMC and historical process knowledge to show that manufacturing is robust, and the process can be improved at the same time
options.D: Internal-external; the MAH itself acts as the RU, with a shared procedure replacing the TT agreement as the main document, and no SU is needed

questions.explanation: Development-commercial TT often begins at Phase 3 and requires the full range of CMC requirements to be transferred, with the goal of establishing comparability of the process or methods between the SU and the RU. Clinical-clinical is a type for which TR65 does not detail the requirements; commercial-commercial applies to marketed products; internal-external is a classification by site type, and the MAH is not the RU.

questions.question: Comparing the three site combinations, which does TR65 consider generally the easiest to manage for knowledge transfer, and why?

options.A: External-external, because both parties are professional CMOs that typically have mature transfer experience and standardized communication patterns
options.B: Internal-external, because the MAH can directly control the external site and can require it to adopt the MAH's own procedures
options.C: Internal-internal, because the same QMS, an integrated document management system, and a standardized TT process generally apply
options.D: The three are about equally difficult; the differences come mainly from the contract value and the seniority of personnel on both sides

questions.explanation: Internal-internal is considered the easiest to manage because the QMS, document management system, and standardized TT process are generally shared, and historical data is easier to obtain. External-external, by contrast, is noted as potentially the biggest challenge, especially when the two external parties do not know each other.

questions.topic: External-external TT - who acts as SU
questions.question: A TT is carried out between two external sites (two different companies) that do not know each other and cannot interact. Who then acts as the SU and facilitates the knowledge transfer?

options.A: The MAH, which must act as the SU itself and facilitate knowledge transfer to the RU
options.B: The RU's TT PM, because it knows best the requirements of the new product and the conditions at the receiving site
options.C: Quality at the original site, because it holds all historical records and deviation investigation data
options.D: The RU's Regulatory, because it knows best the documents and timelines needed for the submission

questions.explanation: When two external parties cannot interact, the MAH needs to play the role of the SU and facilitate knowledge transfer to the RU. TR65 also reminds that the agreement should specify arrangements for MAH and SU SMEs to be on site at the external site.

questions.question: Which sequence is the six-stage TT process described in TR65?

options.A: Initiation, Planning, Readiness, Knowledge Transfer, Execution, Handover
options.B: Initiation, Knowledge Transfer, Planning, Readiness, Handover, Execution
options.C: Initiation, Planning, Knowledge Transfer, Readiness, Execution, Handover
options.D: Planning, Initiation, Knowledge Transfer, Execution, Readiness, Handover

questions.explanation: The six stages are, in order, Initiation, Planning, Knowledge Transfer, Readiness, Execution, and Handover, with a stage gate between each stage. In practice the stages may overlap as business needs require, but the names and sequence are defined this way.

questions.question: How does TR65 describe the members of the TT steering committee?

options.A: Usually one management level above the TT team, with decision-making authority, able to remove obstacles, accept risk, and provide resources
options.B: Usually at the same level as the TT team leads of the functions, so that they can take part in daily execution and handle problems immediately
options.C: Mainly QA personnel from each site, dedicated to reviewing batch records and deciding whether to release the product
options.D: Composed only of MAH Business representatives, because only the MAH is accountable to the regulatory authorities

questions.explanation: The steering committee members are usually one management level above the TT team and have decision-making authority; they remove obstacles, accept risk, provide resources, and judge whether the requirements of each stage have been met. Every participating site should assign a member, not only the MAH or QA.

questions.topic: Scenario - information that changes TT assumptions
questions.question: During a stage, the TT team finds information that could change the boundaries or assumptions of the TT. According to TR65, how should this be handled?

options.A: Assess the impact within the TT team first, and report to the steering committee together at the stage gate of that stage
options.B: Notify the TT PM first, and incorporate the change when the charter is next revised on a regular basis
options.C: Notify Regulatory first, and explain the impact of this information on the application when preparing to file
options.D: Inform the steering committee immediately, without waiting for the stage gate review meeting

questions.explanation: TR65 requires that such information be communicated to the steering committee immediately, rather than waiting for the stage gate review. Because a change in boundaries or assumptions may affect the charter, delayed reporting allows risk to accumulate within the team.

questions.question: After the Planning stage ends, if the TT charter needs to be changed, what does TR65 require?

options.A: Approval by the TT PM is enough, with the change reported to the steering committee afterwards
options.B: It must be approved by the steering committee and documented
options.C: No further changes are allowed; if necessary, the entire project must return to Initiation and start over
options.D: Approved by RU Quality through change control, without involvement of the steering committee

questions.explanation: Charter changes after the Planning stage must be approved by the steering committee and documented. In addition, if the TT success requirements or business assumptions change, the steering committee should re-examine the impact on the Initiation and Planning stages.

questions.question: In addition to the expectations, roles, and responsibilities of each party, which of the following does TR65 recommend that the TT agreement specify explicitly?

options.A: The minimum number of PPQ batches and the acceptance criteria for each batch, and how release is decided
options.B: The version numbers and effective dates of all SOPs, and the format of training records at both ends
options.C: The frequency of supplier qualification audits and auditor qualifications, and the approval process for audit reports
options.D: The units of measure used during the TT, for example mass, temperature, and volume

questions.explanation: In addition to the expectations, roles, and responsibilities, the TT agreement should also specify the units of measure used during the TT (such as mass, temperature, and volume), to avoid misunderstandings caused by different units at the two ends. The number of PPQ batches and acceptance criteria belong in the process VMP and are not requirements of the TT agreement.

questions.question: What is the result of the stage gate of the Initiation stage?

options.A: A decision on whether to proceed with the TT, selection of the RU (often with a signed contract), and approval of the initial TT charter
options.B: Approval of the final charter and detailed project plan, and signing of the TT agreement by the SU, RU, and MAH
options.C: Confirmation that PPQ batch results meet acceptance criteria, and approval of the regulatory submission
options.D: Confirmation that the TT package is complete, and that the RU's facility modifications and equipment qualification are all finished

questions.explanation: The output of the Initiation stage gate is a decision on whether to proceed with the TT, selection of the RU (often with a signed contract), and approval of the initial charter. The final charter and TT agreement are outputs of Planning, the TT package belongs to Knowledge Transfer, and PPQ and the submission belong to Execution.

questions.question: Which function mainly leads the Initiation stage, and what is its core work in this stage?

options.A: RU Manufacturing, which plans operator training and writes the batch record, SOPs, and EHS reports
options.B: SU Process, which writes the process VMP and decides the number of PPQ batches and the sampling plan
options.C: MAH Business, which builds the business case and obtains the QTPP and specifications from the SU
options.D: MAH Quality, which performs the RU audit and approves the TT validation protocols, reports, and release decisions

questions.explanation: The Initiation stage is led by the MAH Business function, which builds the business case and obtains the QTPP and/or specifications from the SU, confirming product characteristics and high-level process requirements as the basis for the product strategy. The process VMP and the number of PPQ batches are addressed later, in the Knowledge Transfer stage.

questions.question: In the Initiation stage, Engineering and other functions jointly perform the facility fit assessment. What is the output of this stage?

options.A: An approved detailed URS and CAR, which can be used directly to place orders with equipment vendors
options.B: A preliminary rough estimate of the capital investment needed for the TT
options.C: Confirmation reports of IQ/OQ completion of the new equipment, for use in PPQ
options.D: The final number of PPQ batches and the sampling plan for each batch

questions.explanation: The facility fit assessment in the Initiation stage covers site utilities and infrastructure, process equipment, and automation capability, and is used to form a preliminary rough estimate of capital needs. The detailed URS and CAR are completed only in the Planning stage.

questions.question: In the Initiation stage, Quality has the potential RU complete a questionnaire and investigates its compliance history. What is the main purpose?

options.A: To approve the RU's PPQ protocol and confirm that the batch record format meets MAH requirements
options.B: To obtain the environmental and occupational permits the RU needs and to estimate the time required to obtain them
options.C: To build a preliminary capacity planning model to evaluate batch size, cycle time, and on-site storage needs
options.D: To judge the maturity of the RU's quality system, its attitude toward GMP, and its level of regulatory compliance

questions.explanation: The purpose of Quality's due diligence is to judge the maturity of the RU's quality system, the organization's mindset toward GMP, and its compliance with applicable regulations, and to provide a compliance risk assessment on that basis. Permit assessment belongs to Manufacturing, and the capacity model belongs to Sourcing/Supply Chain.

questions.topic: Regulatory strategy is a living document
questions.question: Which statement about the initial regulatory strategy drafted in the Initiation stage is correct?

options.A: Once approved in the Initiation stage it is locked, and any later change must return to Initiation for re-approval
options.B: It is updated by Regulatory only once, at the stage gate of the Planning stage, and stays unchanged in the other stages
options.C: It is a living document that should be reviewed and updated at each stage, and the final version may be very different from the first draft
options.D: It need only cover the classification of the planned submission, and need not list the applicable regulations and expected review timelines

questions.explanation: The regulatory strategy is a living document that evolves with the project; it should be reviewed at each stage and updated with new knowledge, and the final version may differ greatly from the first draft. The initial version also includes the market list and submission timeline, applicable regulations, and data requirements, not only the submission classification.

questions.question: At the Planning stage gate, the steering committee approves the final charter and project plan. What does this signify?

options.A: That PPQ results have met acceptance criteria, with agreement to proceed to batch release and subsequent marketing
options.B: That all qualification of the RU's new equipment is complete and the project can enter Execution immediately
options.C: That regulatory approval has been obtained and the product can be formally handed to the commercial operations team
options.D: That the risks defined by the TT are accepted and agreement is given to proceed to the Knowledge Transfer stage

questions.explanation: Approval of the final charter and project plan at the Planning stage gate means that the steering committee accepts the risks defined by the TT and agrees to proceed to Knowledge Transfer. PPQ results, equipment qualification, and regulatory approval all come in later stages.

questions.question: What tool can the TT PM use when negotiating the knowledge transfer roles and responsibilities with the SU and RU, and where are the negotiated results documented?

options.A: An FMEA risk matrix, with the results recorded in an appendix of the process VMP for later reference by validation staff
options.B: A RACI responsibility assignment matrix, recorded in the TT agreement (a shared procedure for internal-internal)
options.C: A Gantt critical path chart, with the results recorded in the success factors of the TT charter as the basis for project progress
options.D: A SIPOC process diagram, with the results recorded in an attachment to the quality agreement, jointly signed by Quality of both parties

questions.explanation: The TT PM can use a RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) matrix to record each party's responsibilities and, after negotiation, document it in the TT agreement; an internal-internal TT can use a shared procedure instead. If the SU and RU are both external parties, the MAH should be listed as a third party.

questions.question: Before Business and the RU sign a supply agreement (such as a Master Service Agreement), what should the TT PM confirm?

options.A: That the contract price is lower than the previous year's budget, with the other terms left to be gradually supplemented and confirmed after the Execution stage
options.B: That the contract batch quantities cover only the initial validation batches, with commercial production contracted separately to preserve negotiating room and flexibility
options.C: That the contract boundaries and assumptions are the same as the TT charter, the RU role is the same as in the TT agreement, and it supports the quality agreement
options.D: That the contract has already been reviewed by the RU's legal department and the TT PM need not review it again, to avoid duplicating Business's work

questions.explanation: TR65 notes that the supply agreement is critical to the TT result, and the TT PM should review it to ensure its boundaries and assumptions are the same as the TT charter, that it is consistent with the RU's roles and responsibilities in the TT agreement, and that it supports the quality agreement. Many RUs also ask the contract to guarantee a fixed number of batches for initial validation and for annual commercial production.

questions.question: In the Planning stage, what does the Process function typically do to demonstrate that the product made by the RU is comparable to the SU's product?

options.A: Draft a comparability plan that lists the information needed to show that the products at the two ends are comparable
options.B: Write the final PPQ report and use its conclusions as proof of comparability
options.C: Approve the URS of the RU's equipment and arrange for the vendor to perform the FAT
options.D: Complete the process VMP and approve the number of PPQ batches and the sampling plan

questions.explanation: In the Planning stage, Process often develops a comparability plan that identifies the information needed to show that the RU's product is comparable to the SU's product. The PPQ report comes after the Execution stage, and the process VMP is written in the Knowledge Transfer stage.

questions.question: The Planning stage best practice recommends forecasting the supply needs for the TT and for initial commercial production as early as possible. What is the approximate time horizon of the forecast?

options.A: About 3 to 6 months
options.B: About 12 to 18 months
options.C: About 24 to 36 months
options.D: About 6 to 9 months

questions.explanation: The best practice recommends forecasting supply needs as early as possible, covering the TT itself and initial post-transfer production, over a horizon of about 12 to 18 months, so that the RU can plan staffing, testing, and document approval in advance and avoid capacity limits later.

questions.question: Why does TR65 ask for particular attention to tacit knowledge in the Knowledge Transfer stage?

options.A: Because explicit knowledge is already fully covered by the TT agreement and no longer needs to be transferred
options.B: Because such information is mostly undocumented and is often discovered only after a failure, yet transferring it offers the greatest room for improvement
options.C: Because regulations require tacit knowledge to be included as an appendix in every TT package
options.D: Because tacit knowledge exists only with RU personnel, and the SU need not participate in this kind of transfer

questions.explanation: Tacit knowledge resides in personnel experience and is often discovered only after a failure, so transferring it can offer the greatest opportunity for improvement. A proactive KM approach allows both explicit (documented) and tacit information to be transferred more effectively.

questions.question: At the stage gate at the end of the Knowledge Transfer stage, what does the steering committee need to confirm?

options.A: That the TT package is complete, and the risks that remain after KT and the corresponding mitigation strategies have been assessed
options.B: That the qualification protocols for all new equipment have been completed and passed, so that PPQ can proceed
options.C: That the engineering batch has been completed and released, and the number of PPQ batches can be decided on that basis
options.D: That the regulatory submission has been approved, so commercial supply and formal handover can begin

questions.explanation: The focus of the KT stage gate is to confirm that the TT package is complete (including the details needed to manufacture, test, and release the product) and to assess the risks remaining after KT and the mitigation strategies. Equipment qualification and the engineering batch belong to Readiness, and regulatory approval comes before Handover.

questions.question: According to TR65, which of the following is part of the content when the process VMP outlines the PPQ requirements?

options.A: The FAT and SAT schedule for the RU facility, the list of acceptance personnel for each piece of equipment, and the vendor's delivery acceptance criteria
options.B: The frequency of supplier audits and auditor qualifications, how audit results are tracked, and the approval process for audit reports
options.C: The content of the PAI storyboard, how mock review question-and-answer roles are divided, and the reception arrangements for reviewers
options.D: The hold-time strategy, permitted rework or reprocessing steps, and the success criteria

questions.explanation: The PPQ requirements in the process VMP cover the process description (including the control strategy and CPPs), batch size and expected yield, the raw material qualification plan, the number of PPQ batches (including matrix or bracketing assumptions), the hold-time strategy, permitted rework or reprocessing, the stability strategy, and the success criteria. FAT/SAT, supplier audits, and the PAI storyboard are not on the list.

questions.question: At the Readiness stage gate, what is the main decision the steering committee makes?

options.A: Approving the final regulatory submission content, and deciding the commercial launch date and first shipment arrangements of the product
options.B: Approving formal handover of the process to the commercial operations team, and ending the TT project with all documents closed
options.C: Judging whether all the requirements for batch execution are in place, and approving the engineering batch
options.D: Approving the result of the RU selection, and agreeing to the content and resource assumptions of the initial TT charter

questions.explanation: The Readiness stage gate is where the steering committee judges whether all the requirements needed for batch execution are in place and approves proceeding with the engineering batch. Selecting the RU is a decision of Initiation, and handover and launch belong to later stages.

questions.question: In the Readiness stage, equipment has completed FAT at the vendor and undergoes SAT after arriving at the RU. Which statement about the capital VMP and the requirements for entering Execution is correct?

options.A: FAT and SAT data may not be referenced and all qualification must be redone at the RU, with PPQ able to run in parallel with qualification
options.B: As long as SAT is passed, equipment and facility modifications can skip qualification and go directly into PPQ
options.C: FAT/SAT is used only for purchasing acceptance and cannot be used to reduce qualification protocol deviations
options.D: The capital VMP often makes use of FAT/SAT data, and new equipment and facility modifications must be completed and pass before Execution

questions.explanation: The capital VMP often uses FAT and/or SAT to reduce qualification protocol deviations or to use their data to satisfy initial qualification requirements. However, qualification of all new equipment and facility modifications must be completed, with all requirements passed, before entering Execution.

questions.question: Under what condition can an engineering batch executed under GMP conditions also serve as a PPQ batch?

options.A: As long as the batch result is better than expected, it can be retroactively accepted as a PPQ batch with approval by the TT PM after batch completion
options.B: It must use material from a different supplier than the one used for PPQ, to widen the coverage and sources of variability in the validation
options.C: When both the pre-approved process VMP and the PPQ protocol allow it, especially when raw material supply is limited
options.D: As long as SU personnel are present throughout and sign a confirmation, it can be relisted as a PPQ batch afterwards and its data used

questions.explanation: If an engineering batch is executed under GMP conditions and both the pre-approved process VMP and the PPQ protocol allow it, it can double as a PPQ batch, especially when raw material supply is limited. TR65 also notes that the engineering run should use the supplier material that will be used for PPQ, not a different supplier.

questions.question: Which statement about TR65's arrangement of stage gates for the Execution stage is correct?

options.A: A single stage gate can be held only once, at the end of Execution, and may not be split into multiple reviews for different activities or added to
options.B: It is held only after a PPQ failure, to decide whether to return to an earlier stage and restart the whole process
options.C: It is chaired by Regulatory after the submission, to confirm the completeness of the application and review progress, and does not involve the process
options.D: Readiness can be confirmed before the engineering run, engineering and process readiness results verified before PPQ, and further gates held afterwards if necessary

questions.explanation: The Execution stage has many activities, and the team can use multiple stage gates: confirming readiness before the engineering run, and verifying the results of engineering and process readiness before PPQ; if the process changes, risks needing mitigation arise, or additional studies are needed, further gates can also be held after the engineering batch and PPQ.

questions.question: In the Execution stage, to prepare for a PAI that may be triggered after the submission, what can Quality do to find problems before filing?

options.A: Conduct a mock inspection (in-depth audit) of the RU
options.B: Repeat all PPQ batches to obtain more data
options.C: Require the RU to perform the facility fit assessment again
options.D: Conduct a supplier qualification audit of the SU

questions.explanation: In the Execution stage, Quality makes final inspection preparations and can perform a mock inspection (in-depth audit) of the RU to find issues that need to be addressed before filing. Whether a PAI is actually triggered depends on the type of TT.

questions.question: At the Handover stage gate, who approves the formal transfer of the process to the RU for routine production?

options.A: Only the TT PM, because the TT PM knows best the completion status of the project
options.B: The steering committee and the RU site management
options.C: MAH Regulatory and SU Quality, because they are responsible for external communication
options.D: The post-transfer operations team, which decides for itself whether to take over

questions.explanation: The Handover stage gate is approved jointly by the steering committee and RU site management, formally handing the process to the RU for routine production. This stage also includes compiling lessons learned, project closure, and document closure.

questions.question: In the Handover stage, which responsibilities for commercial production should RU Manufacturing confirm it is ready to assume?

options.A: Cleaning, product changeover, sampling and sample submission, media fill, change control, maintenance, and batch operations
options.B: Only batch operations and sampling; cleaning and media fill remain the responsibility of the TT team in early commercial production
options.C: Only media fill and product changeover; change control and maintenance continue to be the SU's responsibility
options.D: Only batch operations; the remaining responsibilities are transferred to Quality one by one after regulatory approval

questions.explanation: In the Handover stage, RU Manufacturing must confirm that it is ready to take on all responsibilities once commercial production begins, including cleaning, product changeover, sampling and sample submission, media fill, change control, maintenance activities, and batch operations. TR65 does not reserve any of these for the TT team or the SU.

questions.topic: Source of CPP and QTPP definitions
questions.question: In the TR65 Glossary, from which document are the definitions of Critical Process Parameter and Quality Target Product Profile cited?

options.A: ICH Q10: Pharmaceutical Quality System
options.B: PDA TR54: Implementation of Quality Risk Management
options.C: PDA TR60: Process Validation, A Lifecycle Approach
options.D: ICH Q8(R2): Pharmaceutical Development

questions.explanation: The definitions of CPP and QTPP in the Glossary cite reference (1), which is ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development. ICH Q10 is used in the text to explain the scope of the TT, while TR54 and TR60 are references for quality risk management and process validation respectively.

questions.question: TR65 lists PDA TR54 in its References. What is the subject of this technical report?

options.A: Process Validation, A Lifecycle Approach, focusing on the lifecycle concept of process validation
options.B: Analytical Method Validation and Transfer for Biotechnology Products, aimed at biotechnology products
options.C: Implementation of QRM for Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Manufacturing
options.D: Technology Transfer, 3rd Edition, covering practical approaches and examples of TT

questions.explanation: The subject of TR54 is Implementation of Quality Risk Management for Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Manufacturing Operations. Process Validation, A Lifecycle Approach is TR60, analytical method validation and transfer is TR57, and the Good Practice Guide for TT is published by ISPE.

questions.question: Which document is cited for the definition of Knowledge Management in the Glossary and for the passage on proactive KM in the KT stage?

options.A: ICH Q10: Pharmaceutical Quality System (2008), which also discusses the concept of knowledge management
options.B: Lipa et al.: Effective Knowledge Transfer During Biopharmaceutical TT (JVT 2019)
options.C: ISPE Good Practice Guide: Technology Transfer, 3rd Edition (2018), which contains a KM chapter
options.D: WHO Annex 7: Guidelines on Transfer of Technology (TRS 961), which contains a definition of KM

questions.explanation: The definition of Knowledge Management and the KM discussion in the KT stage cite reference (2), Lipa et al., Effective Knowledge Transfer During Biopharmaceutical Technology Transfer, published in the Journal of Validation Technology in 2019. ICH Q10 is used in the text to explain the scope of the TT.

questions.topic: Note on QRM and retired TR65
questions.question: What does the note after Additional Reading in TR65 say about QRM-specific information for TT and about the retired earlier TR65?

options.A: QRM-specific information is being developed in the PDA QRM series of technical reports; the earlier content can be found at PDA.org and will be removed once the new reports are issued
options.B: QRM-specific information has been fully incorporated into the stage sections of this edition of TR65, so there is no longer any way to look up the earlier edition
options.C: QRM-specific information has been merged into the revised TR54, and the earlier TR65 remains permanently available for download at PDA.org
options.D: QRM-specific information applies only to sterile products and will be replaced by a revision of ICH Q9, which will supersede the earlier content and all its appendices

questions.explanation: The note explains that QRM-specific information for TT is being developed in the PDA QRM technical report series, and the information in the original (retired) TR65 can be found at PDA.org and will be removed once that series of reports is issued.

questions.question: Which of the following documents is a guidance issued by the FDA and listed in the TR65 Additional Reading?

options.A: Q12: Technical and Regulatory Considerations for Pharmaceutical Product Lifecycle Management
options.B: Good Practice Guide: Technology Transfer, 3rd Edition
options.C: Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements
options.D: Reflection Paper on Good Manufacturing Practice and Marketing Authorisation Holders

questions.explanation: Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements is a guidance issued by the FDA in 2016. Q12 is an ICH document, the Good Practice Guide: Technology Transfer is issued by ISPE, and the Reflection Paper is an EMA document.

questions.question: In Case 8.1, Company A kept changing the knowledge requirements, so Company B could not meet the timelines. What measure was then introduced that significantly reduced the change requests?

options.A: Establishing a TT charter, steering committee governance, and a communication plan, and completing the Planning stage activities
options.B: Changing the 15 products to be transferred one at a time in sequence, fully completing one product before starting the next, and suspending all parallel work
options.C: Requiring Company A to station all its staff at Company B and replace Company B's TT PM role and decision-making authority
options.D: Cancelling the weekly cross-functional progress meetings and replacing them with a quarterly meeting between senior executives of both parties with verbal progress tracking

questions.explanation: Case 8.1 introduced a formal TT process, including a steering committee and governance oversight, a communication plan, added staff, and better PM tools. Company B also recognized the value of establishing a charter and completing the Planning stage activities, after which change requests decreased significantly.

questions.question: Case 8.3 is an internal-internal TT. Why does it illustrate that "an internal transfer also needs a full TT process"?

options.A: Because the RU could not obtain the SU's equipment specifications and process documents, so the process could not be replicated at all
options.B: Because it was regarded as low risk, so budget and time were underestimated, the impact of replacement equipment was not assessed, and the SU lacked resources, leaving KT incomplete
options.C: Because the steering committee intervened too much, so the TT team could not decide for itself how to purchase equipment
options.D: Because Regulatory required a new submission for every equipment change, which delayed the project schedule significantly

questions.explanation: In Case 8.3, Company A assessed the risk as low because the equipment and process were similar, and underestimated the budget and time; the same equipment model could not be purchased, so a new model was used without a risk assessment; the SU lacked resources and KT was incomplete. The SU had in fact shared full equipment and process documentation, so "the RU could not obtain equipment specifications and process documents" was not the cause.

questions.question: In Case 8.4, the TT team finally chose CMO F even though its estimated launch timeline was longer. What was the main reason?

options.A: Its cost was clearly lower than CMO E's, and it was willing to take on small veterinary orders
options.B: It was the only one of the three candidates that met the ANVISA requirements for separate lines and separate buildings; the other two did not
options.C: It had considered the complexity of transferring a lyophilized product more thoroughly and had a strong PM, so its timeline assessment was more realistic
options.D: Its estimated launch timeline was the shortest of all candidates, and a lyophilization line was available for immediate use

questions.explanation: The TT team found CMO F's longer timeline more realistic because it had considered the complexity of the lyophilized product transfer in more detail and had a strong PM to guide the process. All three CMOs could meet ANVISA requirements; CMO D was not interested because of the small volumes, and the costs of E and F were similar.

questions.question: In Case 8.9, Company C believed the engineering batch results were poor and it was not advisable to proceed to process validation, while Company A wanted to take the risk and push ahead. What were the compromise and the outcome?

options.A: Company C accepted responsibility for failure and paid for it itself; the validation batches passed on the first attempt, and launch came one month ahead of the original schedule
options.B: Both parties agreed to suspend the project and return to Initiation to select an RU again, with Company B resuming supply
options.C: Company C implemented all improvements in full before proceeding to validation, and the batches passed smoothly, launching on time within 12 months
options.D: Minor improvements and one additional engineering run were made, with Company A accepting the risk; the validation batches failed and the launch was delayed by nearly six months

questions.explanation: The compromise was that Company C would make minor improvements and perform an additional engineering run, proceeding to validation if it went well, with Company A accepting responsibility for any failure. As a result the validation batches failed, three months were lost on investigation and improvement, and the product was launched about six months late.

questions.question: In Case 8.12, what was the main cause of the many downtime events and human errors in early commercial production?

options.A: The PPQ batches did not meet release requirements, but the project went into commercial production with the problems unresolved, causing downtime
options.B: After the project ended, the TT team and consultants left, so no experts were on site, and the SOPs, batch records, and training were insufficient to support production
options.C: The RU began commercial production before obtaining regulatory approval, forcing all batches to be stopped and leading to an inspection
options.D: The SU refused to provide any process data, so the RU's SOPs and batch records could not be fully established and the RU had to find its own way

questions.explanation: In Case 8.12, the commercial batches ran smoothly during the project, but after the project ended the TT team and consultants left, and no experts remained on site. The existing batch records, SOPs, and training were not enough to support production personnel, resulting in downtime, failed batches, and investment loss. The case holds that using the TT Reference Guide could identify key knowledge during the KT stage.
